site_name: Microsoft Fairwater Wisconsin (Mount Pleasant)
load_basis: Not operating in 2025. Epoch AI timeline: Building 1 still not fully operational on 2026-01-28, operational 2026-04-16 at an estimated 369 MW IT (satellite/cooling-based estimate, not a utility figure).
notes: Utility: Microsoft's own project-update page says WE Energies is building a substation on the western part of the parcel, and Microsoft's Sept 2025 blog (https://blogs.microsoft.com/on-the-issues/2025/09/18/made-in-wisconsin-the-worlds-most-powerful-ai-datacenter/) describes a partnership with WE Energies; tariff or contract type was not looked up (price-blind step), so arrangement is left unknown. Year: Epoch lists Building 1 operational 2026-04-16 citing a Microsoft executive post; Microsoft's blog said 'online in early 2026' and WPR (https://www.wpr.org/news/microsoft-pauses-construction-on-parts-of-mount-pleasant-site-again) quotes Microsoft that phase 1 is expected online in 2026. Primary post not viewed directly, hence medium. Planned figure 2,263 MW is Epoch's projected IT power for Q2 2028 (Buildings 1-11); MISO's Dec 2024 new-load list shows 1,480 MW for Microsoft, Mount Pleasant, planned date 2026 (https://cdn.misoenergy.org/NEW%20LOAD%20ANNOUNCEMENTS%20IN%20MISO%20REGIONS%2012062024684954.pdf). Web-search budget was exhausted for this run; all values come from direct fetches of known pages.

site_name: Google Council Bluffs, east buildings at the Bunge Ave campus (10420 Bunge Ave)
load_basis: Epoch AI estimate of IT power for the east buildings: 79 MW from Nov 2024 (Building 1), 158 MW from Jun 2025 (Building 2). Estimate from satellite imagery and cooling equipment, not a utility or operator figure.
notes: IMPORTANT scope caveat: this record is the Epoch entity for the NEW east buildings only. The underlying Bunge Ave campus (Google's second Council Bluffs campus) has been operating far longer: Wikipedia's Council Bluffs article says the second campus on Bunge Avenue held an open house in October 2013 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_Bluffs,_Iowa). If the inventory treats this point as the whole campus, first energization is 2013, not 2024. Epoch's Nov 2024 date for east Building 1 is a stated best guess between generators/cooling installed (Aug 2024) and construction ending (Feb 2025), so 2025 is possible. Building 3 operational Jul 2026 brings Epoch's figure to 237 MW. Utility: Wikipedia's MidAmerican article lists Council Bluffs among the major cities in its service territory and says MidAmerican agreed in 2016 to supply Google's Iowa data centers from Wind XI; no site-specific filing was retrieved. Site address 10420 Bunge Ave, Pottawattamie County, from the Iowa DNR construction application (Questa LLC, facility 78-01-121) cited by Epoch. MISO's Dec 2024 new-load list shows Google, Council Bluffs as 'Existing', 500 MW, which covers all Google campuses there (https://cdn.misoenergy.org/NEW%20LOAD%20ANNOUNCEMENTS%20IN%20MISO%20REGIONS%2012062024684954.pdf).

site_name: Galaxy Helios campus, CoreWeave tenant (984 County Road 112, Afton TX)
operator: Galaxy (Galaxy Helios I LLC), leased to CoreWeave
load_basis: AI data halls were not operating in 2025 (TDLR project start 2025-03-30, completion 2026-06-30; Epoch shows Building 1 operational mid-2026 at an estimated 132 MW IT). The site previously ran as a crypto-mining facility, and its 2025 mining load was not found, so the 2025 site load is left null rather than 0.
notes: Utility NOT found. Galaxy's pages name no retail utility or transmission provider; Galaxy's newsroom lists a Jan 2026 release on completing ERCOT interconnection studies and securing a further 830 MW, for over 1.6 GW approved at Helios (https://www.galaxy.com/newsroom/ and https://www.galaxy.com/data-centers/), which indicates a transmission-level ERCOT interconnection. Our guess (South Plains Electric Coop) and the other candidates (Lighthouse EC, AEP Texas North) are all unconfirmed; investor.galaxy.com refused automated access (403) and was not pursued. Year: Epoch estimates Building 1 at full capacity around Aug 2026 (Galaxy guidance of Phase I by end of H1 2026 plus two months); June 2026 imagery showed it externally complete. Epoch describes the site as retrofitted from a former Galaxy crypto-mining site, so the grid connection itself predates 2026; that earlier year was not sourced here. TCEQ standard-permit review (received 2025-02-06) covers 120 diesel generators, about 251 MW, for Galaxy Helios I LLC, Afton, Dickens County (https://records.tceq.texas.gov/cs/idcplg?IdcService=TCEQ_EXTERNAL_SEARCH_GET_FILE&dID=8711478&Rendition=Web). Planned 528 MW is Epoch's projected IT power for CoreWeave Phases I-III by Q1 2029 (396 MW by Jan 2028); Galaxy's total approved campus power is 1.6+ GW.

notes: Utility and power arrangement NOT found. Nebius's own release (https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-accelerates-us-expansion-adding-up-to-300-mw-capacity-at-new-data-center-in-new-jersey) gives 300 MW phased capacity with first capacity 'as early as summer 2025' and says nothing about power supply; the local news and trade articles Epoch cites refused automated access (403) and were not pursued. Whether the site takes retail service from Vineland Municipal Electric Utility (our smallest-polygon pick), from Atlantic City Electric, or runs partly on on-site generation is therefore undetermined; do not treat the Vineland assignment as verified. Year: SemiAnalysis reports about 25 MW energized by the end of 2025, while Epoch estimates Building 1 operational in early 2026 at 50 MW (https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers/directory/microsoft-nebius-new-jersey), so first power is late 2025 and full phase-one operation is 2026; our 2026 guess is defensible if the inventory wants full-phase operation. Web-search budget was exhausted for this run.
